newsitem.title: USA: Atlas Air eyes freighter options.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Air eyes freighter options.

text.p: Atlas Air, with an eye to lowering its operating costs, is lining up aircraft to replace five Boeing 747-200 freighters leased from Federal Express Corp .

The five, which come off lease next year, are described by Atlas as expensive to operate. Atlas already has leased three 747-200 aircraft for an unidentified source for 1998 delivery as potential replacements for those planes returned to FedEx, chief financial officer Richard Shuyler said in an interview with Reuters.
Alternatively, Atlas could negotiate more favorable lease terms with FedEx, continue flying the five freighters and use the other 747s now being secured for expansion purposes.

Shuyler also confirmed that Atlas is looking into the possibility of acquiring new B-747-400 freighters, which suit the needs of some of Atlas' clients in search of the lower operating costs and extended range capability the 747-400 can deliver.
The list price of a new B-747-400 freighter is in excess of $150 million. Shuyler said no final decision has been made.
"It really comes down to a question of price," he said.
Atlas provides so-called ACMI services - aircraft, crews, maintenance and insureance - to several major airlines on long-term contracts, operating freighters for them under their flight numbers.
By year end, the carrier will have a fleet of 22 B-747-200s. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
